Run arms against a reference

Source: R/core-bench-run.R
hr_benchmark.Rd

Runs every arm on every item of the chosen split(s) of reference, runs times, scores each output with scorer, and returns one row per cluster x item x arm x run. Rows are ordered that way, and the runs are made in the same order.

Usage

hr_benchmark(
  arms,
  reference,
  runs = 5,
  client,
  scorer = hr_scorer_exact(),
  split = "test",
  governor = NULL,
  seed = 1
)

# S3 method for class 'hr_bench'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

arms

An hr_arm() or a list of them, with unique names.

reference

An hr_reference().

runs

How many times each arm runs on each item: a whole number, at least 1. 5 or more is the expected minimum.

client

The client passed to the arms in ctx$client, or NULL for arms that call no model.

scorer

An hr_scorer(); hr_scorer_exact() by default.

split

The split or splits of the reference to run on.

governor

An hr_governor() the whole benchmark is held to, or NULL to take the limits from gr_options().

seed

The seed of the arms' private random stream.

x

An hr_bench.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class hr_bench, a data frame with one row per cluster x item x arm x run and the columns

cluster, item, arm, run, split

Which run of which arm on which item.

correct

TRUE or FALSE, or NA on every run of an item with no label (its failure_kind is still recorded).

outcome

What the scorer saw (see hr_scorer()).

failure_kind

Why a wrong run was wrong: "parse_failure", "refusal", "not_in_document", "wrong", "budget_stop" or "error"; NA when it was correct.

tokens_in, tokens_out, tokens_reasoning, tokens_cached

The run's prompt and reply tokens over its model calls, and the reasoning and cached input tokens among them that the provider reported.

usd

What the run cost, every request priced at its own model, embeddings included, as gr_trace_cost() prices it: 0 for requests a cache or a recording answered, NA when a model has no price.

usd_provenance

Where the token counts the cost rests on came from, over the requests that were paid for: "reported" when the provider reported them all, else "counted" when they were counted with the model's own tokenizer, else "estimated"; "none" when the run paid for no request, and NA when a request does not say.

seconds

The run's wall-clock time.

draw_index

The draw index the run was given: its run number.

ledger_id

The run_id of the run's own trace, which is kept in attr(x, "traces") under that name, and which every step the run added to the benchmark's trace, attr(x, "trace"), carries as ledger_id.

reportable

FALSE for rows on the dev split.

Attributes record the arms (arms: name, version, hash, derived_from), the reference hash, runs, split, seed, the scorer's name, and the traces. print() shows each arm's accuracy over the reportable rows, the mean over runs within each item and then over items, leaving out items with no label; the dev split's accuracy, when there is one, is shown apart in its own column. It adds failures and cost, and is descriptive only: no interval.

Details

Run r of each arm on each item is given ctx$draw_index = r (see hr_arm()), so with the index passed to gr_call() each run is its own entry in a gr_cache() and its own recorded draw in a gr_replay_client(). Each request a run makes with a draw index is recorded under the arm's name as well, so a replay of a benchmark answers each arm with the replies that arm got, even when two arms sent the same request, and whether all the arms are replayed or some, in any order. An arm whose runs are not distinct draws is refused with an error of class hr_duplicate_draw: a run of an arm on an item is a duplicate when one of its requests was answered from a cache or a recording with the same request and draw index as a request of an earlier run, when one of its replies has the provider response id of a reply in an earlier run, or when a recording served a reply without its own draw key (a repeat after the recording ran out of draws, or a recording made without per-draw keys). Every request a run makes should therefore carry the run's draw index. A gr_mock_client() keeps no cache, so under it an arm that leaves the index out is not refused; under a cache it would be.

Every request is checked against governor before it is sent, for the benchmark as a whole: each run's trace is held to the governor's call, spending and token limits less what the runs before it used. A run ends at its first refused request (the hr_budget_refused condition is caught there), is recorded as failure_kind = "budget_stop" and counted wrong (or NA on an item with no label, as below). The runs after it are still started, so every row exists and the refusals are visible; their requests are refused before anything is sent. With governor = NULL the limits are read from gr_options() when the benchmark starts and apply to the whole benchmark, as they apply to one run of a reader. Those defaults are set for one run (400 calls), and a benchmark of two arms on 300 items for 5 runs needs several thousand, so pass a governor sized for the benchmark. When any run is stopped, hr_benchmark() warns (class hr_budget_stopped) with the number of runs stopped, the limits that stopped them, how many of them count against an arm (runs on the dev split or on items with no label do not) and the first run stopped. With governor = NULL it also gives the gr_options() values behind those limits.

An arm that raises an error has that run recorded as "error", counted wrong, with the message in the run's trace. Every run on an item with no label has correct = NA, whatever its failure_kind: a failure on it cannot count against an arm when a success could not count for it. Rows on the "dev" split are marked reportable = FALSE: dev is for tuning, and its scores are not evidence. The reference is locked when scoring starts (see hr_reference()).

Fewer than 5 runs warns (class hr_few_runs): with fewer, run-to-run spread cannot be told from the differences between arms, and interval reports are expected to refuse such a benchmark unless it is labelled descriptive.

The arms run under a private random stream started from seed, so an arm that samples gives the same draws on every call with the same seed, and the caller's random state is left as it was.

See also

hr_arm(), hr_reference(), hr_scorer(), hr_governor()

Other harness: gr_arm(), gr_qa_reference(), gr_scorer_answer(), hr_arm(), hr_contrast(), hr_drift_check(), hr_mdd(), hr_reference(), hr_report(), hr_scorer()

Examples

ref <- hr_reference(
  items = list(q1 = "France", q2 = "Peru", q3 = "Chad", q4 = "Fiji"),
  labels = c("Paris", "Lima", "N'Djamena", "Suva"),
  cluster = c("a", "a", "b", "b"), split = "test")
capitals <- c(France = "Paris", Peru = "Lima", Chad = "Ndjamena", Fiji = "Suva")
cl <- gr_mock_client(function(messages, params) {
  country <- sub("Capital of ", "", messages[[1]]$content)
  capitals[[country]]
})
ask <- hr_arm("ask", function(item, ctx) ctx$call(paste0("Capital of ", item))$text)
bench <- hr_benchmark(ask, ref, runs = 5, client = cl)
bench
#> <hr_bench> 1 arm(s) x 4 item(s) in 2 cluster(s) x 5 run(s); split test; scorer exact_normalised
#>  arm accuracy runs wrong failed budget_stop usd   
#>  ask 0.750    20   5     0      0           0.0000
#>   Descriptive only: accuracy is the mean over runs within each item, then over labelled items, with no interval.
head(bench[, c("item", "run", "correct", "failure_kind", "draw_index")])
#>   item run correct failure_kind draw_index
#> 1   q1   1    TRUE         <NA>          1
#> 2   q1   2    TRUE         <NA>          2
#> 3   q1   3    TRUE         <NA>          3
#> 4   q1   4    TRUE         <NA>          4
#> 5   q1   5    TRUE         <NA>          5
#> 6   q2   1    TRUE         <NA>          1
